summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old female was admitted after an intentional overdose of 20 morphine tablets in the context of severe major depression, chronic abdominal pain from endometriosis, and opiate abuse. She had a history of prior unintentional acetaminophen overdose causing liver injury and pancreatitis, recent breakup, legal issues, and substance use. Initially tearful and depressed, she gradually improved with mirtazapine and quetiapine, discontinued lorazepam, and successfully tapered off narcotics using gabapentin, lidocaine patch, and ibuprofen. A urinary tract infection was treated with Augmentin and resolved. She gained insight into her coping mechanisms, engaged in therapy, and planned to attend a partial hospitalization program. By discharge, her mood was stable, pain was controlled, and she denied suicidal ideation. She was discharged home with her mother, on a regimen of mirtazapine, quetiapine, gabapentin, and other maintenance medications, with follow-up planned.
